claim: Mender's rootfs-image Update Module writes the whole inactive partition in DownloadWithFileSizes (via mender-flash when installed) and only afterwards, in ArtifactInstall, sets mender_boot_part to the new partition with upgrade_available=1 and bootcount=0. So no OneMind trial marker is needed and there is no window in which a power cut boots a new, ungated slot (unlike RAUC, where a pre-install marker is required [C-LAB-rauc-k3s-gate-001]).

rootfs-image ArtifactCommit refuses when upgrade_available is not 1 ('Upgrade failed and was reverted: refusing to commit!'); ArtifactRollback points mender_boot_part back to the other partition and sets upgrade_available=0, and does nothing if the bootloader already rolled back except restore the recorded original partition.

Mender's GRUB integration allows exactly one trial boot: the env is valid only with bootcount 0 or 1; a boot with upgrade_available=1 and bootcount=0 sets bootcount=1 ('Booting new update...'); the next boot with upgrade_available=1 and bootcount!=0 switches mender_boot_part back and clears upgrade_available ('Rolling back...'). OneMind's rule of 3 boot tries (01 §4.2 item 3) therefore needs a modified boot script with Mender.

Mender's GRUB integration keeps two copies of its boot environment, each with a lock file ('editing'), writes them one after the other, and at boot restores a copy whose lock shows an interrupted write from the other copy (RAUC's GRUB backend in the RAUC labs used one grubenv file). [Not exercised by a kill during a bootloader write in this lab.]

mender-convert 5.3.0 pins grub-mender-grubenv at d7c3ec2 and installs the client from https://downloads.mender.io/repos/device-components with APT key fingerprint E6C857345575F9218396566224072B80A1B29B00; that repository's debian/trixie/stable suite (Release dated 2026-10-14) carries mender-update 5.0.2 to 5.2.0-1+debian+trixie, and mender-artifact 4.4.2 is in the workstation-tools repository.

In standalone mode mender-update refuses a new install while an update is in progress ('Update already in progress. Please commit or roll back first'), allows commit only from the commit states, and never reboots the device itself: it reports that a reboot is required and the caller must reboot. The docs require the mender-updated daemon to be stopped, disabled and masked for standalone use.

Mender runs Artifact* state scripts (ArtifactInstall, ArtifactCommit, ArtifactRollback, ArtifactFailure …) only from the artifact itself (stored under the data store's scripts directory at install); /etc/mender/scripts serves only Idle, Sync and Download. In this lab a commit gate placed in /etc/mender/scripts was silently skipped: 'mender-update commit' printed 'Committed.' 4 s after the trial boot's gate started, with no check run and no warning. A Mender health gate must be embedded in every artifact (mender-artifact write -s), or run by the device before it calls commit.

LAB (QEMU x86_64 TCG, Debian 13, k3s v1.37.2+k3s1, Mender 5.2.0 standalone, 2 runs): a good update committed only after the ArtifactCommit_Enter gate saw 3 consecutive fresh k3s passes (run 1 at 86/104/121 s; commit 124 s and 116 s after the gate started) with the broken app in namespace apps not Ready; the next reboot stayed on the new slot.

LAB (2 runs): updates whose k3s exits at start (bad-k3s) or whose kubelet never runs while the API server serves stored status (bad-noagent, the stale-Ready trap) were refused at the 300 s deadline (decided 302-306 s after the gate started, about 330 s after the reboot); Mender's ArtifactRollback reverted the bootloader env at once ('Committing failed. Rolled back.'), the gate rebooted, the box came back on the old slot fresh-healthy, and the failed slot was not selected again.

LAB (2 runs): an update whose init panics (bad-boot) and one that freezes with the watchdog armed (bad-hang) were each booted exactly once; Mender's GRUB script then printed 'Rolling back...' and booted the old slot (98-140 s end to end under TCG); the gate finished Mender's state with 'mender-update rollback'; the failed slot was not tried again. RAUC with HAOS's GRUB logic tries 3 times in the same test [C-LAB-rauc-k3s-gate-009].

LAB (2 runs): QEMU SIGKILL at 16% of Mender's install progress (114 MiB written, about 291 MiB read on the target partition) left the bootloader env unchanged (old slot, upgrade_available=0) and no update in progress; the old slot booted and a reinstall committed. [QEMU kill does not drop the guest's disk caches; real power pulls are founder test F2.]

LAB (2 runs): an artifact signed with a key not in ArtifactVerifyKeys was refused ('Signature verification Error: Wrong manifest signature or wrong key') with the bootloader env and client state unchanged ('No update in progress').

LAB (2 runs, pre-registered prediction H4): a power cut during the first (trial) boot of a good update, after the gate had started, made Mender's GRUB script roll back on the next boot; the box ended committed and fresh-healthy on the old version, but the good update was abandoned and needs a reinstall. RAUC with 3 tries committed the same update on the retry [C-LAB-rauc-k3s-gate-010]. Stock Mender therefore does not meet 01 §4.2 item 3 (3 boot tries) without a boot-script change [untested: founder/lab test F3].

LAB (2 runs): with freshness checks off (API status only), Mender committed a k3s whose kubelet never runs after 3 passes at 60-93 s; localhost:10248/healthz did not answer on the committed slot. The stale-Ready trap is engine-independent (also RAUC [C-LAB-rauc-k3s-gate-008] and Rugix [C-LAB-debian-rugix-023]).
